question: Did the risk of a motorist being killed per mile driven in NYC decline from 2013 to 2025? Make a chart and answer based on this crash data.

options.metric: Annual number of motorist deaths in police-reported crashes
options.reason: A direct count of motorist deaths shows the observed fatal outcome without imposing an unsupported exposure denominator.
options.answer: The per-mile risk cannot be determined because miles driven are absent, but recorded motorist deaths declined from 110 in 2013 to 81 in 2025 (about 26%).
options.interpretation: This framing answers whether the annual number of motorists killed declined: it did between the endpoints, despite substantial year-to-year variation. It is defensible as a direct count of fatal outcomes in the crash file, but it does not measure risk per mile because it has no travel-exposure denominator.

options.metric: Crashes with at least one motorist death per 100,000 police-reported crashes
options.denominator: All police-reported crashes in the same calendar year
options.reason: Normalizing fatal-crash occurrence by all reported crashes provides a crash-based comparison when travel mileage is unavailable.
options.answer: The per-mile risk cannot be determined, but motorist-fatal crashes increased from 50.1 to 87.7 per 100,000 reported crashes between 2013 and 2025 (about 75%).
options.interpretation: This framing answers whether motorist-fatal crashes became more or less frequent relative to all police-reported crashes; the rate is higher at the 2025 endpoint and peaked at 118.0 per 100,000 in 2023. It is defensible as a measure of fatal-crash frequency among recorded crashes, but it leaves per-mile risk unanswered because the denominator is crashes rather than miles driven.

answer:
The per-mile risk cannot be determined because the data contain no miles-driven measure, but recorded motorist deaths fell from 110 in 2013 to 81 in 2025.
The per-mile risk also cannot be determined; motorist-fatal crashes per 100,000 reported crashes rose from 50.1 in 2013 to 87.7 in 2025.
